title: Builder: assemble, then validate once
summary: Each step returns the builder, so optional parts chain in any order. build() rejects a query with no columns and hands back an immutable snapshot that later steps can't change.
code: # Chain optional parts in any order; build() checks them once and returns a finished query.
raise ValueError('select at least one column')
triggers: an object with many optional parts, set in any order, that must be valid once finished
a constructor with a long list of mostly optional parameters
prompts: A report screen lets users pick columns, add any number of filters and optionally cap the row count, in whatever order they click. A report with no columns chosen must be refused before it runs.
A game lets players set up a character across several screens: name, class, starting items. Nothing should exist until the final screen confirms the choices are valid.
invariant: Every step returns the builder; only build() creates a query, after one validation, and the query never shares a list with the builder.
mantra: Set in any order, check once, hand back a copy.
pitfalls: Each step must return self, or the chain breaks at the next call.
Copy lists into the product with tuple(); a shared list lets later steps change a finished query.
Don't name a method after a field: with self.limit as data, a limit() method would be hidden.

anchors.name: Pizza or burger ordering
anchors.trick: Add toppings step by step; build() validates and prices the order.

anchors.name: HTTP client request
anchors.trick: Headers, body and timeout chained before one build().

mutations.explanation: Hands out the builder's own list, so selecting another column later changes a query that was already built.
An empty list is not None, so the check never fires and a query with no columns gets built.
